description: The plot titled “Massive Activation of baseline” illustrates the maximum activation value across different layers of a neural network, comparing four distinct components: attn_output, attn_residual, ffn_output, and ffn_residual. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 22, with tick marks at integer intervals, indicating discrete layer indices. The y-axis, labeled “Max Activation Value,” ranges from 0 to 1600, with major tick marks at intervals of 200. The attn_output (blue dashed line) remains near zero until layer 21, where it rises sharply to about 600. The attn_residual (orange dotted line) exhibits a sharp spike around layer 5, peaking near 1400, then drops to near zero until layer 21, where it surges again to approximately 1600. The ffn_output (green dash-dot line) shows a similar pattern to attn_residual, with a peak near 1400 at layer 5, followed by a dip and a second peak near 1200 at layer 22. The ffn_residual (red solid line) also spikes sharply at layer 5 to about 1400, remains elevated until layer 21, then drops sharply to around 400 at layer 22. All lines exhibit sparse, burst-like activation patterns, with most layers showing near-zero values and only a few layers exhibiting high activation.
